scope: X7-35X QPIC NAND/DMA source correction; physical natural-fault cure remains unproven
corrections: Wait for every prepared command/data/status descriptor under the original shared timeout budget; preserve EOT/FENCE/LOCK/NWD flags.
Synchronize persistent DMA readback for CPU before copying page-scope status; preserve ECC return/accounting and real raw erased-page fallback.
Copy all TX sources including command elements; use isolated RX/status destinations and copy back only after every descriptor completes and unmaps.
On timeout retain the bounded arena, mappings, callback contexts and shared provider/client resource owners; never blindly reset attached hardware or return caller aliases to active DMA.
Reject later preparation, I/O, features and mutable layout/test operations before scratch reuse; blocked legacy commands return FAIL rather than success.
Propagate bad-block-marker read errors rather than claiming a good block; recheck asynchronous poison before reporting feature/ID success.
bounds: Requested allocation cap: 128KiB client dynamic transaction arena including wrappers/vector/bounces; 128KiB provider descriptor allocations; four existing 32KiB hardware FIFOs. Fixed controller/owner/host/SG allocations remain bounded separately by exact geometry. These are not exact slab/RSS measurements.
platform_scope: Independent ownership route only for the built-in exact X7 NAND/BAM node pair, direct DMA with no IOMMU. Ordinary BAM consumers keep original resource ownership. Original platform diagnostic/sysfs identity is retained.
gate_requires: Full actual extracted caller paths, real mapped SG events, delayed/missing completions, every client allocation failure, arena limit, late DMA after caller mutation, TX/command source copies, real provider unissued discard/quota, actual core/client/provider removal with pending refs, MTD unregister refusal, IRQ/callback paths, threaded lifetime races and source-mutation negative controls. Caller-only tests cannot satisfy the strict gate. Complete actual BAM probe and DMA core registration/unregistration; driverless-root registration must fault at runtime in the negative control. The driver-backed registration identity remains distinct from the independently retained allocation/resource owner.
preserved_controls: One-shot probe, original first-failure RAM-only capture, ECC accounting/returns, CPU-cache negative controls, command result/error semantics, non-page-scope, no-status/legacy BAM and ADM controls.
limits: Hardware scheduling/cache/peripheral behavior is simulated by the native harness around actual extracted driver functions. No physical stop/reset proof or natural-fault reproduction is claimed. These source checks do not imply hardware acceptance.
